relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a girl in whom whole exome sequencing found a TNFAIP3 variant: 'The analysis identified a likely pathogenic variant in TNFAIP3'.
method_note: Read the full paper manually; one in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (single unnamed patient of a case report). Table 1 is a single-patient laboratory table, read by hand (no script transcription); a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON. Lab values without stated interpretation or reference range (Hb 10.6 g/dL, ALP 408 U/L, ESR 14 mm/hr) were not recorded as features. Non-TNFAIP3 variants: the paper attributes variants in PIK3R1, HBB and SERPINA1 and a VUS in VPS37A to the patient but prints no descriptions; recorded one row per gene with variant_original_string 'not reported' (the number of variants per gene is not stated). Exon '(5/9)' is printed with the TNFAIP3 variant but has no field. Variant class 'frameshift' taken from the printed 'fs' protein notation; zygosity not stated for this patient (only generic statements about HA20), so 'not reported'. Age at last evaluation recorded as the age at which the girl is described ('5-year-old'); an eight-month follow-up after infliximab followed, so her age at last evaluation may be higher. Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: (1) the title says 'Infantile Onset' but the text gives fever onset 'from age 2' / 'from the age of second year' (the only infantile event is a febrile seizure the authors call possibly coincidental); (2) the TNFAIP3 variant is called 'likely pathogenic' (abstract, case), 'a pathogenic variant' (introduction) and 'probable pathogenic variants' (discussion); recorded 'likely pathogenic'; (3) the PIK3R1/HBB/SERPINA1 variants are 'possibly modifying the phenotype' / 'a potential modifier role' but the discussion says 'They do not modify or explain the core HA20 phenotype'; (4) eye redness, eye pain and eyelid swelling during episodes versus 'ophthalmologic ... investigation ... were negative', so 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' left 'not reported'; (5) abdominal pain, diarrhea and perianal swelling 'resembling hemorrhoidal inflammation' versus negative gastrointestinal investigation and no IBD findings, so 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' left 'not reported'. ANA and celiac serology negative are narrower than the composite 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' item, which is left 'not reported'. CNS involvement marked observed from the infantile febrile convulsive seizure (authors call it possibly comorbid or coincidental). Country from 'this is the first report from northeast of Iran'.
